mechanism_narrative: The recent week-to-week easing of workplace and transit suppression indicates more daily movement capacity, which should lift retail and recreation visits over the next month as commuting-linked discretionary trips recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying above -12 and TRANSIT staying above -33 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If residential time keeps falling while grocery mobility stays positive, households are spending less time at home and more time out, which should translate into a near-term rise in retail and recreation mobility.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0 while GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above 1.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below 5.0 and GROCERY_PHARM stays nonnegative.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in park usage is a leading indicator of broader out-of-home leisure activity, and the sharp reduction in park weakness should spill into retail and recreation within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after a 5-point or larger weekly increase in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: When transit mobility remains deeply depressed, access frictions keep discretionary shopping demand from translating into store visits, so retail and recreation stays below its prior four-week average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean even though TRANSIT stays below -30 for three straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in workplaces and transit signals more synchronized weekday circulation, which should increase retail and recreation spending by raising after-work and lunch-hour stopovers.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT move upward for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If park mobility remains elevated relative to its recent lows, recreational substitution will keep some discretionary trips outdoors and away from shops, reducing retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above -25 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean despite PARKS staying above -25 for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of firmer grocery activity and stable residential time means routine errand bundles are already occurring, and that pattern should spill over into adjacent discretionary retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 1.5 while RESIDENTIAL stays between 5.0 and 6.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM remains above 1.5 and RESIDENTIAL remains near 5 to 6.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, even modest week-on-week gains in workplace mobility should accumulate into more in-person shopping trips, but only if transit is not falling further; otherwise the effect is blocked.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks while TRANSIT does not worsen by more than 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over 28 days despite two consecutive weekly gains in WORKPLACES and no material deterioration in TRANSIT.
